summary: Feasibility decided from the loader source: option A (longer loader watchdog) is impossible (83.88 s is the hardware maximum at 25.6 MHz); option B chosen: the kernel feeds the S5E9945 CL0 watchdog the loader armed, from its existing 10 s heartbeat, only with a timed return and only until loader_return_after + 5 s; the first reload must read back, else nothing is fed and the kernel cuts loader_return_after to 63 s. Kernel built through KRN-044 (STR-041 checks pass, NAT-020 stubs apply). 11 host tests, 17/17 mutants killed. No phone action.
acceptance_assessment: 1 met: README compares A and B with the loader's real constants (guard.c 83 s, WTDAT 65355, prescaler, nat074 30 s pet, final pet) and picks B; one verified stop kept (the watchdog), plus the in-kernel fail-safe cut to 63 s

2 partly, differently: the change is a kernel patch built through the reproducible KRN-044 loop (pinned hashes below), not a loader image; no new image and no heartbeat PID 1 here: the existing hb small root (NAT-100/101) already prints heartbeats; the image is built in NAT-115/116

3 met for the feed: tests read back the constants from the patched source as compiled, mutation pass 17/17; disassembly shows 0x10040000/0x21/0x3f and the dsb; analyser verdicts belong to NAT-116's pass rule (research/notes/NAT-115-post-logo-diagnosis.md)
4 deferred to the image task: the decision draft states the run length 150 s, the cap, what ends a hang, and the pass rule
